author: gmanews
title: Philippines Ranks Second in Southeast Asia for Annual Sleep Loss Due to Warm Nights
text: Philippines Ranks Second in Southeast Asia for Annual Sleep Loss Due to Warm Nights The Philippines and Brunei ranked second in Southeast Asia with 75 hours of sleep lost per person annually due to warmer-than-optimal nighttime temperatures, according to the 2025 Lancet Countdown report. Singapore recorded the highest sleep loss in the region at 81.1 hours, followed by Cambodia at 74.2 hours and Malaysia at 73.9 hours. The indicator is based on over 10 billion sleep observations from fitness trackers between 2015 and 2017 and compares current temperatures to the 1986-2005 baseline. The findings highlight how rising nighttime temperatures affect rest and overall health, while the report notes limitations since fitness tracker users may be wealthier than the general population. Climate change is estimated to account for about 10 percent of annual sleep loss globally. The Philippines tied with Brunei, ranking second among Southeast Asian countries in the average number of sleep hours lost annually due to warmer-than-optimal nighttime temperatures, the latest Lancet Countdown report shows. According to the report's 2025 indicator, each Filipino has lost an estimated 75 hours of sleep every year due to warmer nighttime temperatures, which are not conducive to optimal sleep. Singapore recorded the highest estimated sleep loss in the region at 81.1 hours annually, while Brunei has tied with the Philippines at 75 hours.Other Southeast Asian countries included in the data were Cambodia with 74.2 hours, Malaysia with 73.9 hours, Indonesia with 67.9 hours, Vietnam with 67.1 hours, Myanmar with 64.4 hours, Timor-Leste with 62.2 hours, and Laos with 58.6 hours. Nearly all coral reefs risk collapse in 50 years —IUCN The indicator examines the relationship between warmer nighttime temperatures and sleep loss, using estimates from a multi-country study that analyzed more than 10 billion sleep observations recorded through fitness trackers from 2015 to 2017.It estimates the annual number of sleep hours lost due to nighttime temperatures exceeding the optimal range, compared with the 1986–2005 baseline average. The Lancet Report findings highlight how rising temperatures can affect not only people's health during waking hours but also their ability to get adequate rest at night.It noted limitations in the estimates, including the possibility that the underlying study may not fully represent the wider population, as study participants owned fitness trackers and were likely wealthier than average.that said climate change is costing people nearly 56 hours of sleep per year due to high ambient temperatures in the evenings.\"An estimated six hours of that annual sleep loss, or just over 10%, can be attributed to warming caused by climate change,\" Climate Central said. In its interactive report, Climate Central showed how residents of Las Pinas, Taguig, and Cebu City have experienced 91 hours of heat-related sleep loss annually, while Valenzuela residents have experienced 90 hours of heat-related sleep loss annually.\"The urbanization effect on temperature trends, quantified from satellite night lights, also showed a larger and more significant effect at night than during the day,\" it said. Looking to the long-term temperature data of Metro Manila from 1901-2018, it saw a significance increase in the number of warm nights and a decrease in the number of cool nights as\"materials used in urban areas favor heat retention.\" This is a cause for concern as\"good-quality sleep is essential for physical and mental health,\" the Lancet Countdown said. \"High nighttime temperatures can reduce sleep duration and quality, with consequences for health and wellbeing. \" In the report, the Lancet Countdown acknowledged that the relationship between temperature and sleep may change, as populations learn to adapt to warmer conditions, including through increased access to air conditioning.
summary: Philippines Ranks Second in Southeast Asia for Annual Sleep Loss Due to Warm Nights The Philippines and Brunei ranked second in Southeast Asia with 75 hours of sleep lost per person annually due to warmer-than-optimal nighttime temperatures, according to the 2025 Lancet Countdown report. The findings highlight how rising nighttime temperatures affect rest and overall health, while the report notes limitations since fitness tracker users may be wealthier than the general population.
